title: Signatures from the past
caption: The ESO 3.6-metre telescope and a rock with prehistoric engravings under moonlight, La Silla Observatory
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A red rock fills the foreground, carved with prehistoric engravings, while behind it stands the ESO 3.6-metre telescope at La Silla Observatory in Chile. The Moon dominates the sky and shines brightly enough to light the whole scene.

Several engraved rocks lie around La Silla, and this one belongs to the richest site in the area. A full photographic and topographic survey of the carvings was carried out in 1990. Most show people and animals, along with puzzling geometric figures.

The carvings are believed to be the work of the El Molle complex, northern Chile's first culture. Geologists think the first millennium of our era was much wetter than today, so parts of the Atacama Desert, now very dry, could support settled communities.

understand.summary: This is a moonlit landscape photograph by Babak Tafreshi. The source gives no camera or colour details.
understand.eye: The eye sees little colour in dim light, while a camera can record colour, such as the red of the rock, even in a moonlit scene.
